newsitem.title: GREECE: GREECE CONSIDERS CUTTING CORPORATE TAX RATES - MIN.
newsitem.headline: GREECE CONSIDERS CUTTING CORPORATE TAX RATES - MIN.

text.p: Greece is considering reducing corporate tax rates in an attempt to attract more foreign and European investment and capital, said deputy Finance Minister George Drys.
"The government is seriously considering reducing (current) tax brackets for companies," Drys told Sunday paper 'To Vima'.
Greece, along with Germany and Denmark, has the highest corporate tax rates in the European Union and that must change, he said.

"Given the evolving and continuously increasing competition between the member-states of the European Union to lure capital and investments, Greece will have to adjust its taxation system to the present-day demands of the market, to avoid adverse effects on its economy," Drys said. --Maria Petrakis, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
